items.actClause: AN ACT authorizing the county of Saratoga to transfer and convey reforested lands on Kinns Road to the town of Clifton Park, county of Saratoga
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:  S5813

 TITLE OF BILL :

An act authorizing the county of Saratoga to transfer and convey
reforested lands on Kinns Road to the town of Clifton Park, county of
Saratoga

 PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL :

To ensure the continued use and preservation of Kinns Road Park in the
Town of Clifton Park, Saratoga County.

 SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS :

Section one of the bill authorizes Saratoga County to discontinue the
use of a parcel of reforested land or Kinns Road in the Town of
Clifton Park, and to convey its interest in such land to the Town of
Clifton Park for continued park and recreational purposes. It provides
that the Town shall continue to provide access to such land and
recreational facilities to all county residents. It further provides
that such lands shall be devoted for park and recreational purposes in
perpetuity and the conveyance of such lands shall be done without
compensation and shall riot require any replacement of reforested
lands. Section two identifies the specific parcel of land affected.
Section three provides that the land to be transferred, and all
structures and facilities on such land, shall be maintained, owned and
operated for park purposes by the Town. Section four provides that the
use of such parkland and facilities shall be available to the general
public.

 JUSTIFICATION :

This legislation was requested by both the County of Saratoga and the
Town of Clifton Park. It would provide for the transfer of reforested
lands currently owned by the County to the Town, for use as parklands.
In 1938, the County acquired. a 631/2 acre parcel of land on Kinns
Road in the Town of Clifton Park. Since 1940, this and has been
managed in accordance with the reforested land provisions of Section
219 of the County Law. Beginning in the mid-I970s, there has been
increased interest in the use of such land for park and recreational
purposes. Subsequently, the Town established non-motorized trails and
a picnic area on these lands, and it became commonly known as Kinns
Road Park. The park has become very popular in the community, and the
trails are widely used by hikers, runners and others. A recent plan to
harvest selected timber on the property generated much opposition and
raised concerns about the use and preservation of these lands, which
technically remain "reforested lands." As a result of these concerns,
the County and Town have agreed on a plan to help protect such lands
and ensure their continued use for park and recreational purposes.
This bill is based on previous laws which have authorized the transfer
of parkland from one municipality to another.

 PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY :

2016: S7761; Passed Senate.

 FISCAL IMPLICATIONS FOR STATE AND LOCAL GOVERNMENTS :

None.

 EFFECTIVE DATE :
Immediately.
